headlines.geopolitics: Israeli plan to install Ahmadinejad as Iran's leader revealed
headlines.economy: Bond yields hit highest level since 2007 financial crisis
headlines.domestic: Supreme Court ruling on social media algorithm liability expected

clips.caption: When your Tinder date finds your Reddit history
Duke's wife discovers his secret spending habits
Jax on Americans climbing into monkey enclosures

script.text: I'm not even kidding, she looked at my browser history and said, quote, 'This explains so much about you.'
script.direction: Mortified confession, building to the punchline

script.text: I'm Leo Barros and this is The Friction. Israeli officials reportedly planned to free Iran's former president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad from house arrest as part of a broader regime change strategy.
script.direction: Authoritative news anchor delivery, serious tone

script.text: U.S. officials confirmed the operation was designed to install the hardline former president back in power in Tehran.
The thirty-year U.S. Treasury yield has reached its highest level since two thousand seven, just before the global financial crisis.
script.direction: Steady pace, emphasizing the timeline connection

script.text: Bond yields are elevated across Europe and Asia as inflation fears grip global markets.
The Supreme Court is expected to rule this week on whether social media platforms can be held liable for algorithmic content recommendations that allegedly promote harmful behavior.
The case could fundamentally reshape how platforms like TikTok and YouTube operate.
What's moving markets: The S&P is down two point four percent, dragged by financials after the bond yield spike spooked investors about potential recession risks.
Oil is up three percent to eighty-seven dollars a barrel on Middle East tensions.
Pringle, this Israeli plan to install Ahmadinejad sounds like something out of a Cold War playbook.

Indeed it does, Leo. It bears a striking resemblance to Operation Ajax in nineteen fifty-three, when the CIA and British intelligence orchestrated a coup to remove Iran's democratically elected Prime Minister Mohammad Mossadegh.
script.direction: Scholarly but engaging, drawing the parallel clearly

script.text: They installed the Shah, thinking they'd get a reliable Western ally. Instead, they created the conditions for the nineteen seventy-nine Islamic Revolution.
So regime change operations have a history of unintended consequences in Iran specifically.
Precisely. The Shah's authoritarian rule, propped up by Western intelligence, directly led to the anti-American sentiment that brought Ayatollah Khomeini to power.
And now we're potentially looking at another attempt to reshape Iran's government from the outside.
History suggests that foreign-installed leaders often become either tyrants or martyrs. Rarely do they become the stable allies their sponsors hoped for.
script.direction: Delivering the historical wisdom with authority

script.text: We'll be right back with The Hangout.
Alright, we're back. So Israel wants to install Ahmadinejad, who was already a hardliner when he was president.
Wait, aren't we usually trying to get rid of hardliners, not put them back in power?
The logic seems to be that he'd be so unpopular, it would destabilize the current regime.
That's like trying to fix your relationship by sleeping with your ex to make your girlfriend jealous. Technically a strategy, but...
script.direction: Building up the analogy with comedic timing

script.text: That is oddly specific, Jax.
Okay, so I may have tried something similar recently. Not the ex thing, but like, strategic chaos.
script.direction: Reluctant admission, setting up the story

script.text: I'm talking to this girl on the apps, right? And she's way out of my league, like embarrassingly so.
So I figure, maybe if I show her how terrible other guys are, I'll look better by comparison.
Oh no. What did you do?
I sent her screenshots of the worst pickup lines other guys had sent me on dating apps. You know, like a public service.
Wait, other guys send you pickup lines?
I may have accidentally set my profile to 'looking for everyone' instead of just women. Anyway, not the point.
So I'm showing her these terrible messages, thinking I'm being helpful, demonstrating my value as a decent human being.
script.direction: Still thinking this was a good plan

script.text: And she goes, 'Why do you have so many of these?' So I had to explain about my dating app settings mishap.
Then she asks to see my browser history to make sure I'm not some kind of weird catfish collector.
I'm not even kidding, she looked at my browser history and said, quote, 'This explains so much about you.'
script.direction: Mortified confession, building to the punchline

script.text: What was in there?
Apparently I Google 'how to tell if cat is judging me' more than most people Google anything else.
Ha! That's actually kind of sweet though.
She unmatched me immediately after seeing that I'd researched 'can cats sense desperation' fourteen times last month.
Sounds like your regime change operation backfired spectacularly.
script.direction: Dryly connecting it back to the news

script.text: Speaking of backfiring, Jenny found out about my secret gas station purchases last week.
Secret gas station purchases?
She put me on a strict snack budget after I spent sixty dollars on beef jerky in one week.
So I started paying cash for my gas station runs and telling her I was just getting gas.
Except she noticed I was filling up every other day but never driving anywhere.
Turns out she'd been tracking my location and knew I was spending twenty minutes at the Speedway buying Slim Jims like some kind of processed meat addict.
Dude, that's like surveillance state level stuff.
She said I violated the 'financial transparency clause' of our marriage. I didn't even know we had clauses.
And on that note of domestic surveillance...
Before we go, some Americans got arrested for climbing into a baby monkey's enclosure at a Tokyo zoo.
Apparently the monkey went viral on social media and they wanted selfies.
We're really out here risking international incidents for TikTok content.
script.direction: Exasperated commentary on social media culture

script.text: Also, someone intentionally drove their Cybertruck into a lake to test something called 'Wade Mode.'
It did not work. The truck is now a very expensive artificial reef.
I understood approximately none of that, but it sounds expensive.
That's The Friction. I'm Leo Barros, still trying to understand strategic chaos.
Haywood Pringle, grateful my dating years predate browser histories.
Duke Patel, currently under financial surveillance.
And Jax Mooney, still being judged by my cat. We'll see you tomorrow.
